newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's release of B Band bids delayed to June.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's release of B Band bids delayed to June.

text.p: The Brazilian government has delayed until June the planned release of the qualifying bids for B Band frequency cellular concessions, a Communications Ministry spokesman said.
"They will only be released after the minister gets back from Europe and he is scheduled to return on June 2," the spokesman said.
Communications Minister Sergio Motta heads for Portugal tonight to sign a contract for the laying of a cable under the Atlantic linking Brazil with its former colonial master.
The cable project is the result of a partnership between Portugal Telecom and Brazilian long-distance monopoly Embratel, a unit of the federal Telebras system.
In April, 15 foreign and local consortia presented bids for nine of 10 B Band concessions offered by the government, the first move towards opening of Brazil's coveted cellular telephone sector.
The government had been expected to make the qualified offers public sometime between May 15 and May 20 and sign all concession contracts with private operators by early July.
The privatization is expected to rake in some $5 billion in fees for Brazil.
